audit.primary_source_citation: Barahona JD, Yang L, Nelson DM, Yokoyama WM. "TGF-beta drives the conversion of conventional NK cells into uterine tissue-resident NK cells to support murine pregnancy." eLife 2026;15:RP109878. doi:10.7554/eLife.109878. PMID 42417504; PMC13345626. Preprint: bioRxiv 2025.11.18.688992, PMID 41332720 / PMC12667894 (full text archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/T2_PMC12667894.txt). PRIORITY CORRECTION: this is NOT the first source for the lineage claim. The cNK-origin of uterine trNK was first asserted from primary data by Tatematsu BK & Sojka DK, "Tissue-resident natural killer cells derived from conventional natural killer cells are regulated by progesterone in the uterus", Mucosal Immunol 2025;18:390-401, PMID 39708955 (online 19 Dec 2024), using parabiosis + intravascular labelling in VIRGIN mice; that paper is paywalled (not OA, no PMC) and I could obtain only the abstract, so its methods are NOT audited here. Barahona 2026 is the first ADOPTIVE-TRANSFER demonstration and the first during pregnancy, which is why it is graded as the primary source for the claim as worded.
audit.fulltext_unavailable_reason: Full Materials and Methods obtained for the graded primary source (bioRxiv/PMC12667894 OA full text + eLife VOR methods). Two adjacent sources could NOT be obtained in full: Tatematsu & Sojka, Mucosal Immunol 2025 (PMID 39708955) is paywalled with no PMC deposit — WebFetch on doi.org and on the Elsevier linkinghub URL both returned only redirect/consent shells, so only the abstract was read; and the eLife public reviews were only obtainable in summarised form via WebFetch, not verbatim.
audit.species: Mus musculus. C57BL/6 (CD45.2) and B6.SJL-Ptprc-a/BoyJ (CD45.1) from Charles River; Ncr1-iCre (gift of E. Vivier) crossed to B6;129-Tgfbr2-tm1Karl/J (JAX 012603) to generate TGF-betaRII-Ncr1-delta and littermate controls. Females 6-8 weeks old, timed-mated to C57BL/6-CD45.1 males (plug = gd0.5).
audit.what_was_measured: In mice, 2.5x10^6 negatively-selected CD45.2+ splenic cNK cells (gated CD3-CD19-NK1.1+NKp46+CD49b+; stated purity 87-93%) were injected i.v. via tail vein into pregnant C57BL/6-CD45.1 dams at gestational day 0.5; at gd10.5 individual implantation sites were Liberase TL/DNase-digested and the surface/intranuclear phenotype (CD49a, CD49b, Eomes, NK1.1, NKp46) of donor-derived CD45.1-negative CD45.2+ cells was read out by flow cytometry with Precision Count Beads, in n=4 pregnant dams; a subset of donor cells scored CD49a+CD49b-Eomes+. In parallel, at gd6.5/10.5/14.5 an i.v. anti-CD45.2-PE-Cy7 pulse 3 min before euthanasia was used to score which uterine NK populations were intravascular versus extravascular, and TGF-betaRII surface staining was compared between splenic and uterine cNK. Separately, absolute number and frequency of CD49a+Eomes+ trNK, CD49a+Eomes- ILC1 and CD49b+Eomes+ cNK in gd10.5 implantation sites were compared between TGF-betaRII-Ncr1-delta dams and littermate controls, and 3.0x10^6 purified CD45.1+ cNK (vs HBSS vehicle) were transferred into pregnant TGF-betaRII-Ncr1-delta dams at gd0.5 (n=3 reconstituted vs n=4 vehicle). Pregnancy readouts at gd10.5 were implantation-site count, resorption rate, and blinded stereological measurement of decidual spiral artery lumen area and wall thickness on Masson's-trichrome midsagittal sections (>=4 implantation sites per litter).
audit.n: 4 pregnant dams for the core adoptive-transfer experiment (gd0.5 transfer, gd10.5 readout). 3 reconstituted vs 4 HBSS-vehicle dams for the cNK reconstitution of TGF-betaRII-Ncr1-delta dams. Group sizes for the TGF-betaRII-Ncr1-delta vs littermate-control comparisons are not stated in the Methods text and are reported only in figure panels; the paper states only that sample sizes were set for alpha=0.5 (sic, likely typo for 0.05) and 85% power. No number of independent experimental replicates is given for the transfer.
audit.n_unit: pregnant dams (individual mice); NOT cells. Histology additionally aggregated >=4 implantation sites per litter within each dam.
audit.controls: (1) Congenic CD45.1/CD45.2 discrimination of donor from host cells; (2) dams mated to CD45.1 MALES so that fetal lymphocytes at the maternal-fetal interface are excluded from the maternal donor gate; (3) i.v. anti-CD45.2-PE-Cy7 3 min pre-euthanasia to exclude blood-borne cells from the tissue-resident gate; (4) Cre-negative/flox littermate controls for TGF-betaRII-Ncr1-delta (reviewers additionally prompted separate characterisation of Ncr1-iCre-only controls); (5) HBSS vehicle-only controls for the reconstitution arm; (6) splenic cNK numbers/frequencies compared between genotypes as an internal specificity control (unchanged); (7) blinding of investigators to genotype during spiral artery morphometry; (8) fixable viability dye and 2.4G2 Fc block. MISSING controls: no no-transfer/isotype-transfer baseline for the donor gate; no pre-transfer CD49a/Eomes staining of the actual inoculum reported (only CD49b+ purity 87-93%); no proliferation dye (CFSE/CTV) or Ki67 to separate conversion from selective expansion; no clonal/barcode or genetic fate-mapping label; no non-pregnant/virgin transfer arm in this paper.
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: Selection and expansion of a pre-existing convertible/committed minority within the inoculum, not conversion of a bona fide conventional NK cell. The transferred population was negatively selected to only 87-93% purity, i.e. up to 13% of 2.5x10^6 = up to ~325,000 injected cells were NOT the intended CD3-CD19-NK1.1+NKp46+CD49b+ cNK, and the paper reports no pre-transfer CD49a/Eomes profile of the inoculum. Only "very few" donor cells were recovered from the uterus (eLife Reviewer #2's phrasing), so a rare pre-existing CD49a+ trNK-like cell, an NK precursor, or a CD49b+ subset already licensed for residency, selectively retained and locally expanded in the uterine niche, would generate an identical CD49a+CD49b-Eomes+ donor readout with no conversion having occurred. Nothing in the design excludes this: there is no proliferation dye, no Ki67, no clonal barcode and no intermediate timepoint between gd0.5 and gd10.5, and Sojka et al. J Immunol 2018 (PMID 30275046) independently showed uterine trNK proliferate locally during decidualization, which is exactly the amplification step selection would exploit. Reviewer #2 raised this directly, asking whether "only a specific subset of (splenic) cNK [is] capable of differentiating into trNK". A second, separate alternative applies to the genetic arm: eLife Reviewer #1 noted that the accumulation of CD49b+ cNK in the TGF-betaRII-Ncr1-delta uterus "suggests a defect in tissue retention rather than recruitment" — since Ncr1-iCre deletes in ALL NKp46+ cells including established uterine trNK and ILC1, the reduced trNK number is equally consistent with failure to MAINTAIN a resident population as with a blocked cNK-to-trNK conversion. Finally, the entire endpoint is INF_MARKER-grade: "trNK" here is defined solely by CD49a+CD49b-Eomes+ plus exclusion from the i.v. label, with no function, no transcriptome, and (contrary to the task hint) no CD9 and no CD69 measured on the donor cells.
audit.counter_evidence: Substantial and partly from the same lab. (1) Chiossone L et al., Haematologica 2014;99:448-457, PMID 24179150 — the direct contradiction: transfer experiments from EGFP+ mice into pregnant mice showed that peripheral MATURE NK cells "did not migrate into decidua and uterus", while only NK PRECURSORS were recruited and differentiated in situ; they identified proliferating immature NK precursors in decidua/uterus as early as gd4.5. This is the same experimental design as Barahona's with the opposite result. (2) Sojka DK et al., eLife 2014;3:e01659, PMID 24714492 — from Yokoyama's own lab, concluded uterine trNK are a SEPARATE LINEAGE from cNK: uterine trNK persist in NFIL3-deficient mice in which cNK are absent, and persist in T-bet-deficient mice, i.e. two genetic dissociations from the cNK lineage; their uterine parabiosis at 2 weeks also found host CD49a+DX5- trNK to be overwhelmingly host-derived despite near-complete splenic chimerism. The 2026 paper does not address the NFIL3 result. (3) Chantakru S et al., J Immunol 2002;168:22-28, PMID 11751942 — orthotopic uterine grafts plus transfers of thymus/BM/LN/spleen cells into NK-deficient recipients supported "precursor cell recruitment", not conversion of mature cNK. (4) Sojka DK et al., J Immunol 2018;201:2551-2556, PMID 30275046 — local proliferation of resident uterine trNK during decidualization, i.e. the expansion-of-pre-existing-cells alternative. (5) Vacca P et al., PNAS 2011;108:2402-2407, PMID 21248224 — human decidual CD34+ hematopoietic precursors differentiate into NK cells on stromal contact: a second, independent local origin. (6) The human corroboration the paper leans on (recipient-genotype uNK after uterus transplantation; bioRxiv 2024.03.04.583277, still a preprint) shows blood-borne replenishment but cannot distinguish a mature cNK converting from a circulating precursor seeding, so it does not resolve the same ambiguity.
audit.downstream_dependency: Concrete named dependencies: (a) Registry claim T3 ("Peripheral blood NK -> decidual NK-like", currently graded IN VITRO ONLY on Keskin 2007 PMID 17360654 / Cerdeira 2013) — Barahona 2026 is the ONLY in vivo TGF-beta-driven evidence that would license upgrading T3 out of the in vitro-only class, and the paper explicitly invokes Keskin as the conserved human counterpart. If T2's transfer is really selection, T3 stays in vitro-only. (b) Registry claim T1 ("cNK -> trNK, acquisition of a residency phenotype", currently MIXED) — T2 is the per-tissue instance carrying the "adoptive transfer for" side of T1. (c) Within the primary source itself, the causal attribution of the TGF-betaRII-Ncr1-delta pregnancy phenotype (37% reduction in decidual spiral artery luminal area, 75% increase in wall thickness, increased gd10.5 resorption, reduced litter size at first parturition) specifically to failed cNK-to-trNK conversion — an attribution that is confounded because the same knockout also markedly depletes uterine ILC1s. (d) Registry claim R3 (TGF-beta withdrawal reverts residency) presupposes TGF-beta as the residency-imposing signal that T2 establishes in the uterus. Graded MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the claim is only ~1 year old (Dec 2024 parabiosis, 2026 transfer), rests on one lab-pair, and the older reproductive-immunology literature (Chantakru 2002, Chiossone 2014) still supports a competing precursor-recruitment model that remains widely cited.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: The classification survives, the attribution and the framing do not. UPHELD: the citation exists and OBS_TRANSFER is the correct strongest class — Barahona et al. did transfer sorted splenic cNK into pregnant congenic dams and recover donor cells with a uterine trNK surface phenotype, in vivo. OVERTURNED/CORRECTED on five points. (1) AUTHOR MISATTRIBUTION: the author is Josselyn D. Barahona (WashU, Yokoyama lab), not "Barahona Ponce"; Carol Barahona Ponce is a gallbladder-cancer geneticist with no NK work — my first search on the hint name returned only endometrial-cancer PDX and ESHG abstracts. (2) PRIORITY: Barahona/Yokoyama did not first establish the claim. Tatematsu & Sojka, Mucosal Immunol 2025 (PMID 39708955, online Dec 2024) asserted cNK-derived uterine trNK first, from parabiosis in virgin mice, and Barahona's own earlier J Immunol 2025 paper (PMID 40725997) inferred a cNK-lineage origin from an Eomes requirement — an INF_MARKER/OBS_GENETIC inference, not a lineage observation. (3) The "requires TGF-betaRII" clause is a SEPARATE evidence class (OBS_GENETIC, Ncr1-iCre x Tgfbr2-fl) and is NOT part of the transfer; it also does not test conversion specifically, because Ncr1-iCre deletes in resident trNK/ILC1 as well as in incoming cNK, so loss of maintenance is an equally good reading (raised by eLife Reviewer #1 as a "tissue retention rather than recruitment" defect). (4) The hint's expected markers are wrong: CD9 was NOT measured anywhere in the paper, and neither was CD69; the entire donor readout is CD49a/CD49b/Eomes plus an i.v. CD45.2 label. Recipients were immunocompetent C57BL/6-CD45.1 dams, NOT Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- alymphoid hosts. (5) MOST IMPORTANT: the evidence is population-level, n=4 dams, single 10-day interval, 87-93% inoculum purity, no clonal or barcode label and no proliferation tracking, so it does not exclude the canonical alternative that a pre-existing convertible minority was selected and expanded — and there is direct published contradiction (Chiossone 2014: transferred mature peripheral NK did NOT enter decidua/uterus; Sojka 2014, same Yokoyama lab: uterine trNK survive NFIL3 deficiency that ablates cNK, therefore a distinct lineage). The claim should be recorded as OBS_TRANSFER (weak, single-study, contradicted), not as settled lineage fact.
audit.methods_quote: "Wildtype CD45.2 splenic cNK cells were purified by negative selection (Stem Cell Technologies, Vancouver, Canada) to obtain CD3-CD19-NK1.1+NKp46+CD49b+ cNK cells with purity of 87-93%. 2.5x10^6 purified CD45.2+ cNK cells were injected intravascularly via tail vein injection into C57BL/6 CD45.1 pregnant dams at gd 0.5. The phenotype of adoptively transferred cNK cells was then assessed by flow cytometry at gd 10.5." (Materials and Methods, "cNK Cell Adoptive Transfer Studies in Pregnant Dams"). Gating definition: "Maternal uterine trNK cells were defined as viable singlets, CD3-CD19-CD45.1-CD45.2+NK1.1+NKp46+CD49a+CD49b-Eomes+." Result statement: "By gd 10.5, a subset of adoptively transferred splenic cNK cells upregulated CD49a and downregulated CD49b, acquiring a phenotype characteristic of CD49a+Eomes+ uterine trNK cells." From the eLife version of record, Figure 5 reconstitution: "3.0x10^6 purified CD45.1+ cNK cells were suspended in 300 uL of sterile Hank's Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS) and injected intravascularly via tail vein injection into pregnant TGF-betaRII-Ncr1-delta dams at gd 0.5" (reconstituted n=3, HBSS controls n=4).

NOT-FOUND vs NOT-SEARCHED bookkeeping (rule G3): I SEARCHED and could not find any "Barahona Ponce" NK/uterine paper - that name does not exist in this literature and the hint is a misattribution of Josselyn D. Barahona. I SEARCHED and could not find any published uterine-NK adoptive transfer into Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- recipients in the graded paper (recipients were immunocompetent congenic CD45.1 dams); Chantakru 2002 is the paper that used alymphoid Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- recipients, but transferred bulk thymus/BM/LN/spleen cells, not sorted cNK. I SEARCHED and could not obtain the Tatematsu & Sojka 2025 methods (paywalled, no PMC) - its parabiosis n, chimerism percentage and marker panel are therefore UNVERIFIED by me and I have not graded it. I did NOT independently verify the eLife public reviews verbatim; they reached me only through WebFetch summarisation, so the reviewer quotes above should be treated as second-hand. Additional context worth carrying forward: the Barahona intravascular-labelling result (extravascular CD49b+Eomes+ cNK inside implantation sites rising from gd6.5 to gd14.5) is INF_KINETIC on its own and is the softest link in the argument chain, since it establishes only that cNK enter the uterus, not that they convert. Sparano et al. JEM 2025 (PMID 39692745) provides an adjacent autocrine-TGF-beta1 requirement for virgin-uterus resident NK and is worth a separate row; note it is a maintenance requirement, not a conversion observation. Finally, note the direct intra-lab reversal for the audit trail: Yokoyama's lab published in 2014 that uterine trNK are a lineage distinct from cNK (NFIL3-independent) and in 2026 that uterine trNK are converted cNK; the 2026 paper does not reconcile the NFIL3 data.

adv.challenge_reason:
I re-read the Methods myself (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/T2_PMC12667894.txt = bioRxiv/PMC12667894 full Materials and Methods; plus targeted WebFetch of the eLife VOR at elifesciences.org/articles/109878). Three of the auditor's facts are confirmed and one is fabricated-by-inference; the evidence list is over-credited.

CONFIRMED: transfer of 2.5x10^6 negatively-selected CD3-CD19-NK1.1+NKp46+CD49b+ splenic CD45.2 cNK (purity 87-93%) i.v. into C57BL/6-CD45.1 pregnant dams at gd0.5, phenotype read at gd10.5, n=4 dams (Fig 1C-D legend, VOR); reconstitution arm 3.0x10^6 CD45.1+ cNK into TGF-betaRII-Ncr1-delta dams, n=3, 25 implantation sites (Fig 5, VOR only — this experiment is NOT in the preprint); antibody panel is CD3e/CD19/CD45.1/CD45.2/CD49a/CD49b/Eomes/NK1.1/NKp46/TGF-betaRII — no CD9, no CD69, confirming the auditor's rebuttal of the task hint.

FABRICATED CONTROL (the auditor's control #3): the row credits the transfer with "i.v. anti-CD45.2-PE-Cy7 3 min pre-euthanasia to exclude blood-borne cells from the tissue-resident gate." This is false. The Methods sentence "To distinguish tissue-resident lymphocytes at the maternal-fetal interface from those in circulation, we administered 3 ug of fluorescently labeled anti-CD45.2-PE-Cy7 (104)..." applies ONLY to the endogenous-cell experiments (Fig 1A-B). It was NOT applied to transfer recipients, and it CANNOT be: the i.v. label is anti-CD45.2 clone 104, which is the very marker that defines the donor gate (donor CD45.2 into CD45.1 host), so an i.v. CD45.2 pulse would label every circulating donor cell and collide with the ex vivo CD45.2 stain. Consequence: RESIDENCY WAS NEVER MEASURED ON THE DONOR CELLS. The "tissue-resident" half of "B" rests entirely on CD49a+CD49b-Eomes+ staining of cells liberated by Liberase digestion of whole implantation sites — which includes the uterine vasculature.

OVER-CREDITED CLASS — strike OBS_GENETIC: the spec's OBS_GENETIC is "knock out gene, B fails to appear," and it must be lineage-informative. Ncr1-iCre x Tgfbr2-fl deletes TGF-betaRII in ALL NKp46+ cells — incoming cNK, established uterine trNK, and ILC1 alike — so reduced trNK is equally explained by failed maintenance/retention of a resident population. The mechanism's home field settles this: Zhang & Bevan, Immunity 2013 (PMID 24076049) showed TGF-beta signalling controls gut TRM "by regulating migration and retention," and Ma et al., J Immunol 2017 (PMID 27903738) showed TGF-beta promotes kidney-resident T cell formation by enhancing selectin/chemokine-mediated EXTRAVASATION of effectors — i.e. a Tgfbr2 conditional KO reducing tissue-resident numbers is the expected result even with zero effect on differentiation. Barahona measured no entry, no retention and no proliferation readout in the KO. Torcellan et al., Immunity 2024 (PMID 38157853) additionally showed conditional Tgfbr2 deletion does NOT impair skin trNK formation while it IS required for salivary-gland trNK — the same genetic manipulation gives opposite answers in two tissues, so it is not a generic "conversion switch."

ALSO NOT REPORTED BY THE PAPER: no quantification of the fraction of donor cells that converted (Fig 1 gives no percentage or absolute number); no pre-transfer CD49a/Eomes profile of the inoculum; no Ki67/CFSE/CellTrace; no barcode or clonal label; no intermediate timepoint between gd0.5 and gd10.5.

NO UPGRADE AVAILABLE: I looked specifically for a genuine fate-map. There is none. Ncr1-iCre is used purely as a deleter, not as a lineage reporter. No OBS_DIRECT.

NET VERDICT: DOWNGRADE. OBS_TRANSFER survives as the strongest class in the letter of the spec (congenic donor cells were transferred and recovered), but it is OBS_TRANSFER with a purely marker-defined, unquantified, residency-untested endpoint, and OBS_GENETIC must come off the list. G7 applies: what the methods did is "recover congenically marked donor cells bearing three TGF-beta-inducible markers from digested implantation sites," not "observe a conventional NK cell become a tissue-resident NK cell."
adv.revised_evidence_type_strongest: OBS_TRANSFER — retained as strongest class, but downgraded in weight: congenic (CD45.1/CD45.2) adoptive transfer with donor recovery, endpoint defined ONLY by CD49a+CD49b-Eomes+ surface/intranuclear staining, with residency of donor cells never tested (no intravascular label applied to transfer recipients), no conversion frequency reported, n=4 dams, single 10-day interval. Revised evidence_types_all: [OBS_TRANSFER (weak, marker-endpoint), INF_MARKER, INF_KINETIC (the gd6.5->gd14.5 rise in extravascular CD49b+Eomes+ cNK, which shows only entry, not conversion)]. STRIKE OBS_GENETIC — the Ncr1-iCre x Tgfbr2-fl arm deletes in the resident target population as well as the putative precursor and is confounded by TGF-beta's established roles in extravasation and retention, so it carries no lineage information for "A becomes B."
adv.new_counter_evidence: Four items the prior auditor missed, two of them decisive. (1) Flommersfeld S et al., Immunity 2021;54:2288-2304, PMID 34437840 (full text archived /home/user/aaa/refs/T2_PMC8528403.txt) — THE NAMED PRE-EXISTING SUBSET. Retrogenic colour-barcode fate mapping of SINGLE NK cells plus congenic parabiosis identified "two distinct NK cell lineages present already during the steady state and stably maintained throughout infection." The second is a CD27+CD62L-CD160+ "ILC1-like NK" population that is Eomes+, NK1.1+, NKp46+, CD69+, "expressed CD49b (albeit less than CD62L+ subsets), and, like these, lacked CD49a," and by parabiosis "remained almost entirely spleen resident, while cNK cells equilibrated between the two parabionts." This is exactly the cell Barahona's CD3-CD19-NK1.1+NKp46+CD49b+ negative-selection inoculum co-purifies: Eomes+, CD49a-negative at the time of transfer, already carrying a residency programme, and a lineage that does NOT interconvert with cNK. Its CD49a-upregulating progeny would score identically in Barahona's donor gate with no cNK-to-trNK conversion having occurred. The auditor gestured at "a rare pre-existing CD49a+ trNK-like cell" but never named this population or this paper. (2) Torcellan T et al., Immunity 2024;57:124-140, PMID 38157853 (archived T2_PMC10783803.txt) — cited in Barahona's own reference list, and it indicts Barahona's assay by name: "The tracking and manipulation of NK cells... have been largely limited to adoptive transfer approaches... This approach bears the caveat of co-transferring progenitor populations and spleen-resident ILC-like NK cells, which may confound the cellular origin of the cells engrafting into tissues." They therefore replaced transfer with inducible genetic fate mapping (Sell-CreERT2 and Eomes-CreERT2 x Rosa26-LSL-tdTomato) plus percutaneous Dendra2 photoconversion, which simultaneously proved residency AND excluded proliferative dilution. Barahona did none of this. Torcellan also found salivary-gland trNK develop independently of cNK and of Eomes, i.e. two independent trNK origins within one animal. (3) Boulenouar S et al., Front Immunol 2016;7:43, PMID 26925058 (archived T2_PMC4759249.txt) — the PREGNANCY-SPECIFIC NFIL3 contradiction, far more damaging than the auditor's Sojka 2014. In Nfil3-/- dams (cNK development crippled), uterine CD49a+Eomes+ trNK expanded about sevenfold during pregnancy, "nearly as extensive as in pregnant WT mice," while uterine CD49a-DX5+ cNK "did not expand at all" (vs 3.7-fold in WT). Pregnancy-associated accumulation of uterine trNK therefore proceeds essentially normally when the putative circulating source is absent. The same paper also destroys the gating premise: "The expression of CD49a and DX5 has been described as mutually exclusive on the two subsets both in liver and uterus; however, we found that DX5 was expressed on most uterine CD49a+ cells" — so CD49a+CD49b- is not a clean partition in the uterus, and DX5/CD49b levels are themselves NFIL3- and context-regulated. (4) Filipovic I et al., Nat Commun 2018;9:4492, PMID 30374017 (archived T2_PMC6206068.txt) — a genuine genetic fate map of the uterus that Barahona ignores: Rorc(RORgt)-fate-map YFP+ cells are present among uterine group 1 ILCs, "aligned with 'ex-ILC3s' described in other tissues," i.e. a THIRD, ILC3-derived origin; and uterine trNK are Ki67-high at gd9.5, the local-proliferation route. Also, the eLife public reviews (obtained only via WebFetch summarisation, NOT verbatim — same limitation the prior auditor flagged) state that reviewers asked whether "only a specific subset of (splenic) cNK [is] capable of differentiating into trNK," raised "local proliferation of cNK-derived trNK," noted only "very few cells can be detected within the uterus," and asked that the "conversion" conclusion be "toned down"; the authors' revised text concedes cNK entering the uterine vasculature "may fail to acquire molecular programs required for residency and instead continue to transit." The auditor's Chiossone 2014 (PMID 24179150), Sojka 2014 (PMID 24714492), Chantakru 2002 (PMID 11751942), Sojka 2018 (PMID 30275046) and Vacca 2011 (PMID 21248224) all stand as cited.
adv.crossfield_g4_findings:
The mechanism invoked is circulating-to-resident conversion under TGF-beta. Three home fields have already run this argument and each returns a lesson that Barahona's design fails.

T CELL / TRM. (a) SELECTION WAS THE ANSWER LAST TIME. Mackay LK et al., Nat Immunol 2013;14:1294-1301, PMID 24162776, "The developmental pathway for CD103+CD8+ tissue-resident memory T cells of skin": skin TRM do not arise from bulk effectors — they arise from a PRE-EXISTING KLRG1-negative subset, with KLRG1+ effectors largely excluded. The field that invented the transfer-and-recover assay discovered, using that assay plus subset fractionation, that the apparent conversion was selection of a minority already licensed for residency. Barahona transferred an unfractionated 87-93%-pure bulk inoculum with no pre-transfer phenotype and no subset fractionation, so it sits on the wrong side of exactly this lesson. (b) TGF-beta IS A TRAFFICKING AND RETENTION SIGNAL, NOT ONLY A DIFFERENTIATION SIGNAL. Zhang N & Bevan MJ, Immunity 2013;39:687-696, PMID 24076049: TGF-beta controls formation AND maintenance of gut TRM "by regulating migration and retention." Ma C et al., J Immunol 2017;198:749-756, PMID 27903738: TGF-beta promotes kidney-resident T cell formation by enhancing E-/P-selectin- and chemokine-mediated EXTRAVASATION of effector T cells — it acts at the tissue-ENTRY checkpoint. A Tgfbr2 conditional knockout that reduces resident-phenotype cells is therefore the null expectation under trafficking/retention alone. Barahona's KO arm has no entry, retention or proliferation readout, and its most striking result — uterine CD49b+Eomes+ cNK ACCUMULATE while trNK fall — is the classic signature of cells arriving but not being retained. (c) RESIDENCY MUST BE MEASURED, NOT INFERRED FROM MARKERS. Skon CN et al., Nat Immunol 2013;14:1285-1293, PMID 24162775 (S1pr1 downregulation is required for residency) and Anderson KG et al., Nat Protoc 2014;9:209-222, PMID 24385150 (intravascular staining as the field standard) set the bar. Barahona applied the intravascular standard to endogenous cells only and NOT to the donor cells — the one place the claim needed it. (d) WHAT PARABIOSIS CANNOT PROVE — bears directly on the priority source. Parabiosis measures exchange of a labelled compartment. Blood carries NK and ILC precursors as well as mature cNK, so partner-derived cells acquiring a trNK phenotype in a parabiont are equally consistent with precursor seeding. Tatematsu & Sojka 2025 (PMID 39708955), the priority claimant, is a parabiosis + intravascular-label study and is therefore intrinsically unable to discriminate mature-cNK conversion from precursor recruitment — precisely the model that Chiossone 2014 (PMID 24179150) and Vacca 2011 (PMID 21248224) support for the uterus.

ILC. (e) Flommersfeld 2021 (PMID 34437840) as above: two pre-existing, non-interconverting NK lineages in the steady-state spleen, one of them spleen-RESIDENT, Eomes+, CD69+, CD49b-positive-but-low, CD49a-negative — a named, characterised candidate for the "convertible minority" in Barahona's inoculum, established by single-cell barcoding, the strongest available lineage method. (f) Zeis P et al., Immunity 2020;53:775-792, PMID 33002412, "In Situ Maturation and Tissue Adaptation of Type 2 Innate Lymphoid Cell Progenitors": ILC progenitors seed tissues and mature IN SITU, acquiring tissue-specific phenotypes — the ILC-field version of precursor seeding, which reproduces a "circulating-cell-becomes-resident-phenotype" readout with no mature-cell conversion. (g) THE ENDPOINT MARKERS ARE GENERIC. Gao Y et al., Nat Immunol 2017;18:1004-1015, PMID 28759001 and Cortez VS et al., Nat Immunol 2017;18:995-1003, PMID 28759002 established that TGF-beta/SMAD signalling drives cNK toward a CD49a+ ILC1-like state in tumours, and Cortez 2016 (PMID 27156386) in salivary gland; Cuff 2019 (PMID 31572388) in obese liver. CD49a-up/CD49b-down/Eomes-retained is a generic TGF-beta response readable in at least four unrelated tissues, so it identifies a TGF-beta-exposed NK cell, not a uterine trNK. This is why the endpoint is INF_MARKER-grade. (h) Torcellan 2024: Tgfbr2 deletion blocks salivary-gland trNK but NOT skin trNK — tissue-specific, so the Tgfbr2 result cannot be generalised into a conversion mechanism.

MYELOID — THE HARDEST LESSON. (i) Ginhoux F et al., Science 2010;330:841-845, PMID 20966214 and Hashimoto D et al., Immunity 2013;38:792-804, PMID 23601688: genetic fate mapping overturned decades of transfer- and chimerism-based dogma that blood monocytes generate tissue macrophages; most resident macrophages are embryonically seeded and self-renew locally. Transfer-plus-phenotype was the assay that got it wrong, and fate mapping was the assay that fixed it. (j) Guilliams M & Scott CL, Nat Rev Immunol 2017;17:451-460, PMID 28461703, "Does niche competition determine the origin of tissue-resident macrophages?" — the decisive methodological point. When a resident niche is empty or expanding, circulating cells fill it and adopt the FULL resident transcriptional and phenotypic identity. Therefore "transfer A, recover something with B's phenotype" demonstrates niche PERMISSIVENESS, not steady-state ontogeny. Two direct applications: the gd0.5-to-gd10.5 uterus is a rapidly expanding, largely unfilled niche, so donor filling and local phenotypic imprinting is the expected outcome under BOTH the conversion model and the precursor-recruitment model; and in TGF-betaRII-Ncr1-delta dams the accumulation of uterine cNK alongside loss of trNK is exactly what an unfilled/unretained niche looks like.

BOTTOM LINE FROM THE HOME FIELDS: the assays that settled this question elsewhere are inducible genetic fate mapping (Sell/Eomes-CreERT2, KLRG1-CreERT2, Cx3cr1-CreERT2), single-cell barcoding, photoconversion, and intravascular labelling of the tracked cells. Barahona used none of them on the donor population. Every field that relied on bulk transfer plus marker phenotype was later corrected, in the same direction: what looked like conversion was selection of a pre-existing subset, or seeding of a precursor into an empty niche.

adv.load_bearing_reason:
MEDIUM is the right level, but the auditor anchored it on the wrong things. Three of its four named dependencies (registry claims T1, T3, R3) are internal to this very audit registry — a claim cannot be load-bearing chiefly because other rows in the same spreadsheet point at it. That is circular and should not count. Substituting concrete, external, named dependencies:

(1) TGF-beta-RESISTANT NK CELL ENGINEERING. The premise that TGF-beta converts circulating cNK into a tissue-resident/ILC1-like, non-cytotoxic state in vivo is the stated rationale for dominant-negative TGF-betaRII and TGFBR2-knockout CAR-NK constructs, built directly on Gao et al., Nat Immunol 2017 (PMID 28759001) and Cortez et al., Nat Immunol 2017 (PMID 28759002). Barahona 2026 is now the in vivo, non-tumour, physiological instance of that axis and is invoked in its own Discussion as showing "this same signaling axis" operating in tumour, obese liver and uterus. If the uterine result is selection of a pre-existing TGF-beta-primed minority (Flommersfeld PMID 34437840) rather than conversion of bulk cNK, the generalisation weakens.

(2) PERIPHERAL-BLOOD NK TESTING IN REPRODUCTIVE MEDICINE. The clinical practice of measuring peripheral blood NK number/cytotoxicity as a proxy for uterine NK in recurrent miscarriage and recurrent implantation failure — the subject of Von Woon E et al., Hum Reprod Update 2022;28:548-582, PMID 35265977, which Barahona cites — presupposes that circulating NK cells are the source pool for uterine NK. Under the competing distinct-lineage/local-precursor model (Sojka 2014 PMID 24714492; Boulenouar 2016 PMID 26925058; Vacca 2011 PMID 21248224), that proxy has no mechanistic basis. This is a real, funded, patient-facing dependency.

(3) THE PAPER'S OWN CAUSAL ATTRIBUTION. The 37% reduction in decidual spiral artery luminal area, 75% increase in wall thickness, increased gd10.5 resorption and reduced litter size in TGF-betaRII-Ncr1-delta dams are attributed specifically to failed cNK-to-trNK conversion. That attribution is confounded twice over: the same Cre also markedly depletes uterine ILC1s (the authors' rebuttal rests on their own earlier Eomes-Ncr1-delta paper, PMID 40725997), and TGF-beta's established roles in extravasation and retention (PMIDs 24076049, 27903738) supply a conversion-free explanation for the whole phenotype.

(4) THE HUMAN CONSERVATION ARGUMENT. Keskin et al., PNAS 2007 (PMID 17360654) is in vitro only; Strunz et al., Sci Immunol 2021 (PMID 33617461) proposes continuous human uNK differentiation; the uterus-transplantation recipient-genotype result the paper leans on is still an unpeer-reviewed preprint (bioRxiv 2024.03.04.583277) and, like parabiosis, cannot separate a converting mature cNK from a seeding circulating precursor. So the human arm supplies no independent support.

Not HIGH: the VOR is ~1 month old (eLife, 8 July 2026), essentially uncited, from a single lab pair, and its own reviewers asked for the "conversion" conclusion to be toned down. Not LOW: dependency (2) is genuine clinical practice and dependency (1) is an active translational programme, both of which would need re-argument if the uterine result is selection rather than conversion.
adv.better_primary_source:
No better AUDITABLE primary source exists for the uterine claim as worded, and I am recording two distinct G3 outcomes.

SEARCHED AND COULD NOT OBTAIN: Tatematsu BK & Sojka DK, Mucosal Immunol 2025;18:390-401, PMID 39708955, doi 10.1016/j.mucimm.2024.12.009 (online 19 Dec 2024) retains PRIORITY for first asserting cNK-derived uterine trNK from primary data (parabiosis + intravascular labelling in virgin mice). I re-attempted the full text at mucosalimmunology.org/article/S1933-0219(24)00132-6/fulltext and received a hard HTTP 403 Forbidden — note this differs from the prior auditor's report of a "redirect/consent shell," so the block is a server-side refusal, not a cookie wall. Its parabiosis n, pair duration, chimerism percentages and marker panel remain UNVERIFIED and I have not graded it. Crucially, even if obtained, its design is parabiosis, which cannot discriminate mature-cNK conversion from circulating-precursor seeding (see G4 finding d), so it would not be a stronger primary source than Barahona — it would be a differently weak one. I did NOT attempt sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1933021924001326 or institutional/interlibrary routes: NOT_SEARCHED.

BETTER PRIMARY SOURCE FOR THE GENERAL MECHANISM (circulating cNK -> tissue-resident NK), and the correct methodological benchmark this claim should be graded against: Torcellan T, Friedrich C, et al., "Circulating NK cells establish tissue residency upon acute infection of skin and mediate accelerated effector responses to secondary infection," Immunity 2024;57:124-140, PMID 38157853, PMC10783803 (OA full text archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/T2_PMC10783803.txt). This is OBS_DIRECT-grade: inducible genetic fate mapping of endogenous, untouched cells (Sell-CreERT2 x Rosa26-LSL-tdTomato and Eomes-CreERT2 x Rosa26-LSL-tdTomato, tamoxifen before infection) plus non-invasive percutaneous Dendra2 photoswitching that proved both residency and absence of proliferative dilution, plus intravascular CD45 labelling and an IFN-gamma-eGFP-CreERT2 fate map. It is skin, not uterus, so it does not establish T2 — but it demonstrates that the uterine claim could have been tested at OBS_DIRECT level with existing, published tools and was not, and it explicitly names the flaw in the assay that was used instead ("co-transferring progenitor populations and spleen-resident ILC-like NK cells... may confound the cellular origin"). It also contradicts a general TGF-beta requirement (Tgfbr2 deletion did not affect skin trNK formation).

EARLIEST TRANSFER-INTO-UTERUS PRIMARY SOURCE, for the audit trail: Chantakru S et al., J Immunol 2002;168:22-28, PMID 11751942 (archived T2_11751942.txt) — orthotopic uterine grafts plus transfers of thymus/BM/LN/spleen cells into alymphoid Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- recipients. It predates every claimant here and its authors concluded PRECURSOR RECRUITMENT, not conversion of mature cNK. Also note for the audit trail: Filipovic 2018 (PMID 30374017) is the only genuine genetic fate-mapping study performed in the mouse uterus in this literature (Rorc-YFP), and it points to a third, ILC3-derived contribution that Barahona does not address.

final.resolution_note: OBS_TRANSFER — retained as strongest class, but downgraded in weight: congenic (CD45.1/CD45.2) adoptive transfer with donor recovery, endpoint defined ONLY by CD49a+CD49b-Eomes+ surface/intranuclear staining, with residency of donor cells never tested (no intravascular label applied to transfer recipients), no conversion frequency reported, n=4 dams, single 10-day interval.
